mainTopic: Proof that a bride married as a בתולה, and why the משנה about רבי יהושע uses the father's field (חזקה and protest)
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier discussion: for someone who taught Torah to others, there is no limit to the honor at his funeral. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a woman who says she married as a בתולה. It gives two explanations of the הינומא. It then explains that roasted grain was proof in יהודה, while in בבל the sign was smearing oil on the heads of the Sages. A widow's wedding had no roasted grain. Next, the גמרא asks why the משנה about רבי יהושע speaks of a field that belonged to the other person's father and not to the other person himself. It answers that only the father's field allows a real middle case: two years of use in the father's lifetime and one in the minor son's, which is no חזקה according to רב הונא. Along the way, the גמרא proves from the משנה of the three lands that a protest made away from the holder still counts, as רבי אבא בר ממל explains it. The amud ends with a question on his answer, which is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: No limit on honor at the funeral of one who taught Torah
steps.stepSummary: The earlier discussion ends: for a person who taught others, there is no set measure for the honor at his funeral.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for someone who taught others, there is no limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion about how many people must stop to honor a Torah scholar at his funeral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, a set number of people was given for someone who learned Torah himself. Here the גמרא adds that someone who also taught others has no upper limit. Everyone should honor him.
steps.whatToRemember: Teaching Torah to others earns unlimited honor at one's funeral.

phrases.english: But for one who teaches others,
there is no limit for him.
phrases.notes: This closes the earlier talk about how many people should come to honor a scholar's funeral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For one who teaches Torah, there is no limit to the honor given at his funeral.

steps.title: What is a הינומא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about witnesses who saw the bride go out with a הינומא and asks what that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If there are witnesses that she went out with a הינומא...' What is a הינומא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks what the word הינומא means. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, witnesses who saw a הינומא at the wedding prove the woman married as a בתולה, so her כתובה is two hundred. To use that proof, we need to know what a הינומא actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: A wedding item used for a בְּתוּלָה bride. Its exact meaning is discussed here.

phrases.english: And if there are witnesses
that she went out with a hinnuma, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. 'Went out' means she left her father's house to go to the wedding.

phrases.english: What is a hinnuma?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word הינומא.

steps.title: A canopy of myrtle
steps.stepSummary: סורחב בר פפא, in the name of זעירי, says a הינומא is a canopy made of myrtle.
steps.simpleTranslation: סורחב בר פפא said in the name of זעירי: it is a canopy of myrtle.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: a הינומא is a canopy of myrtle branches over the bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, the witnesses saw a myrtle canopy at the wedding. That was a sign of a בתולה's wedding.

phrases.aramaic: סוּרְחַב בַּר פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּזְעֵירִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Surḥav bar Pappa said in the name of Ze'eiri:
A canopy of myrtle.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּרְחַב בַּר פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּזְעֵירִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הינומא is a canopy of myrtle.

steps.title: A veil the bride dozes under
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a הינומא is a veil under which the bride dozes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is a veil that the bride dozes under.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: רבי יוחנן says a הינומא is a veil over the bride's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different explanation, not a rejection of the first. Instead of a canopy over her, it is a cloth covering her face. It looks as if she is dozing beneath it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A veil under which the bride dozes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הינומא is a veil covering the bride's face.

steps.title: Roasted grain is proof in יהודה, but what about בבל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא and a ברייתא saying roasted grain was proof in יהודה, then asks what the sign was in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says, etc. It was taught: in יהודה this is proof. What about in בבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. It notes that the roasted-grain custom was a sign only in יהודה, and asks what the sign was in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says that even handing out roasted grain at the wedding proves she was a בתולה. A ברייתא limits this to יהודה, where that was the custom. So the גמרא asks which custom in בבל would serve as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A תַּנָּא quoted in the מִשְׁנָה
It was taught (introduces a teaching from the time of the מִשְׁנָה)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה's full line: even handing out roasted grain at the wedding is proof she was a virgin.

phrases.english: It was taught: in Judea it is proof,
In Babylonia, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What wedding custom in בבל showed that the bride was a בתולה.

steps.title: In Babylonia: oil smeared on the Sages' heads
steps.stepSummary: רב says that in בבל the sign was smearing oil on the heads of the Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: smearing oil on the heads of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers: at a בתולה's wedding in בבל, they smeared oil on the heads of the Sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who saw this custom at the wedding would prove she married as a בתולה. It does the same job as roasted grain in יהודה.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Smearing of oil on the heads of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about בבל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Smearing oil on the Sages' heads was the sign in בבל.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: is this shampoo oil?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, who does not know this custom, asks אביי whether it means oil used for washing hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Are you saying oil for washing hair?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא doesn't understand what kind of oil-smearing רב meant. He asks אביי if it is just hair-washing oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא is asking for clarity. He doesn't recognize a special wedding custom, so he wonders whether this is simply ordinary hair oil.

keyTerms.meaning: Master (a polite way to address a teacher)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Is the Master saying oil for shampooing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רב's answer means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of oil-smearing רב meant.

steps.title: אביי: didn't your own mother do this at your wedding?
steps.stepSummary: אביי calls רב פפא 'orphan' and tells him this was done at his own wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Orphan! Didn't your mother arrange oil-smearing on the Sages' heads at your own wedding?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that this is a known wedding custom. It was even done at רב פפא's own wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי shows it is not ordinary hair oil but a set wedding custom. Calling רב פפא 'orphan' is a jab at how he could not know a custom his own family carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of the event (the wedding)

phrases.english: He said to him: Orphan,
didn't your mother do for you
smearing of oil on the heads of the Sages
at the time of the event?
phrases.notes: The 'event' here means his own wedding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: This is a known wedding custom, not plain hair oil.

steps.title: A story showing the oil custom at a wedding
steps.stepSummary: A story tells of a wedding between a scholar's family and רבה בר עולא's family, where oil was smeared on the Sages' heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of a certain scholar who arranged a marriage for his son into the family of רבה בר עולא. Some say it was רבה בר עולא who arranged a marriage for his son into the family of a certain scholar. And he smeared oil on the heads of the Sages at the wedding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי with a real case where this oil custom was done at a wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who married into whose family, but both agree on the key point. Oil was smeared on the Sages' heads at the wedding, so the custom was real.

phrases.english: Like that case of a certain one of the Sages
who arranged a marriage for his son
into the family of Rabba bar Ulla,
and some say,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא אִיעֲסַק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla arranged a marriage for his son
into the family of a certain one of the Sages,
and he smeared oil on the heads of the Sages
at the time of the event.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That smearing oil on the Sages' heads was a real wedding custom.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A wedding involving רבה בר עולא's family.
steps.whatToRemember: In בבל, smearing oil on the Sages' heads marked a בתולה's wedding, just as roasted grain did in יהודה.

steps.title: What about a widow's wedding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the custom is at an אלמנה's wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a widow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a widow's wedding is different. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since these customs mark a בתולה's wedding, we need to know what is missing at an אלמנה's wedding. That difference is what lets witnesses tell the two apart.

phrases.english: A widow, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from a בתולה's wedding to a widow's wedding.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What custom applies, or is missing, at a widow's wedding.

steps.title: A widow has no roasted grain
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that roasted grain is not handed out at a widow's wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: a widow does not have roasted grain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that roasted grain is not handed out at a widow's wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why roasted grain works as proof. It is done only for a בתולה, so seeing it shows the bride was not a widow.

keyTerms.meaning: Roasted grain (קְלָיוֹת) handed out at a wedding

steps.whatToRemember: Roasted grain is given only at a בתולה's wedding, never a widow's, which is why it can serve as proof.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
A widow does not have roasted grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about a widow.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No roasted grain is handed out at a widow's wedding.

steps.title: Why not use the simpler case of 'your own field'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about רבי יהושע admitting in a field case. It asks why the משנה did not give the simpler example of a field that belonged to the other person himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And רבי יהושע admits in the case of one who says to his fellow,' and so on. But then let the משנה say: 'רבי יהושע admits in the case of one who says to his fellow: This field was yours, and I bought it from you!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks a question about its wording. Why did the משנה pick a field that belonged to the other person's father, and not to the other person himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a man admits the field used to belong to his friend's father but says he bought it. He is believed, because the same mouth that gave the bad news gave the good news. The גמרא asks why the משנה used the father's field, when the same idea would work just as well with a field that belonged to the friend himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Admits, agrees. Here, רבי יהושע agrees in this case even though he disagrees elsewhere.
To his fellow, to another person
Etc., and so on. The גמרא quotes only the start of the line.
But let it teach. This asks why the משנה did not use different wording.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua concedes
in a case where one says to his fellow, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is: 'This field was your father's, and I bought it from him.' He is believed.

phrases.english: But let it teach: Rabbi Yehoshua concedes
in a case where one says to his fellow:
This field was yours,
and I bought it from you?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיתְנֵי: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ שָׂדֶה זוֹ שֶׁלְּךָ הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wedding customs discussion and moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice of the 'father's field' example
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'your own field' case seems simpler and teaches the same rule, so why use the father's field?

steps.title: The משנה chose the father's field because of its last clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה used the father's field so it could add a last clause: if witnesses show the field was the father's, the man is not believed when he says he bought it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wanted to teach the last clause: 'If there are witnesses that it was his father's, and he says, I bought it from him, he is not believed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The משנה chose the father's field because of the clause that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause of the משנה says that once witnesses prove the field was the father's, the man's claim of buying it is no longer believed. The man's own mouth is no longer the only source of the bad news. The גמרא is saying this clause fits only the father's case. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה

phrases.english: Because he wanted
phrases.notes: 'He' means the author of the משנה.

phrases.english: to teach the last clause:
If there are witnesses that it was his,
and he says: 'I bought it from him'
he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording is needed for a later clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could just as well have used 'your own field.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The father's field was chosen so the witnesses clause could be added.

steps.title: Why the witnesses clause can't work for 'your own field'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that with 'your own field,' the witnesses clause makes no sense. If the man used the field for the years of חזקה, he should be believed. If he did not, it is too obvious to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would the case be? If he used the field for the years of חזקה, why is he not believed?! And if he did not use it for the years of חזקה, it is obvious that he is not believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining why the witnesses clause only fits the father's field. It tests the 'your own field' case both ways, and both ways fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who openly uses a field for the years of חזקה is believed when he says he bought it, even without a document. So in that case, 'not believed' would be wrong. If he did not use it that long, then of course he is not believed, and the משנה would not need to say so. Either way, the 'your own field' version of the clause does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
The years of חזקה: the period of open use that shows ownership

steps.confusionAlert: This step is still part of the answer, not a new challenge. It explains why the משנה avoided 'your own field.'

phrases.english: What would the case be?
phrases.notes: He means: if the משנה had said 'your own field.'

phrases.english: If he used it for the years of presumptive ownership,
phrases.notes: Literally 'ate it.' He ate the field's crops, meaning he openly used the land.

phrases.english: why is he not believed?!
And if he did not use it for the years of presumptive ownership,
it is obvious that he is not believed!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי דְּאַכְלַהּ שְׁנֵי חֲזָקָה אַמַּאי לָא מְהֵימַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the answer of step 13 by showing the 'your own field' case fails both ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: For 'your own field,' the witnesses clause is either wrong or too obvious to teach.

steps.title: The same problem applies to the father's field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the same two-sided test seems to work against the father's field too. So why is the father's case any better?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same applies to his father's field: if he used it for the years of חזקה, why is he not believed?! And if he did not use it for the years of חזקה, it is obvious that he is not believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The same test seems to knock out the father's field case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on the father's field being different from 'your own field.' But the same reasoning about the years of חזקה seems to apply to both. If so, the answer did not really explain why the משנה chose the father's field, and the original question returns.

phrases.english: If so, regarding his father too:
if he used it for the years of presumptive ownership,
why is he not believed?!
And if he did not use it for the years of presumptive ownership,
it is obvious that he is not believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the reasoning of step 14 against the answer given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the witnesses clause works only for the father's field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'used it for the years of חזקה or not' test makes the father's case fail too, so the two cases are no different.

steps.title: The father's field allows a split case: two years with the father, one with the son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that with a father's field there is a real middle case. The holder ate the field two years in the father's lifetime and one year in the son's. Following רב הונא, the son's year does not count, so there is no חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine with the father's case, because you can find a situation like this: the holder ate the field's produce for two years while the father was alive and one year while the son had it. This follows רב הונא, who said: You cannot make a חזקה on a minor's property, even after he grows up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 15. It shows that the father's field allows a case that is neither obvious nor automatically a valid חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the two-sided test said: either the holder had three years, so he should be believed, or he did not, so the case is obvious. The father's field adds a third option. There were three full years of use, but one was on a minor's property, and under רב הונא that year does not count. So the witnesses clause teaches something real.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine / granted (this side works)
You can find a case for it
You cannot make a חזקה (a claim of ownership by use)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה chose the father's field. The case of 'your own field' cannot produce this in-between situation.
steps.confusionAlert: The holder really did use the field for three years. He loses only because one of those years was on a minor's property, and that year does not count.

phrases.english: It is fine regarding his father, you can find it,
for example, where he ate it two years in the father's lifetime,
phrases.notes: 'Ate it' means he used the field and ate its produce. These are two of the three years needed for a חזקה.

phrases.english: and one in the lifetime of his son,
and in line with רב הונא.
For רב הונא said:
One cannot make a חזקה on a minor's property,
even if he grew up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by finding a middle case that only the father's field allows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a specific case that escapes the two-sided test
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same either-or test seems to make the father's case pointless too.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the father's field, two years with the father and one with the minor son gives three years of use but no חזקה, so the witnesses clause teaches something new.

steps.title: Did רב הונא just repeat the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה already shows this case, why would רב הונא need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And did רב הונא come to teach us a משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. Our משנה already seems to contain his rule, so what did he add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only way to explain the משנה is the split case of step 16, then the משנה already teaches that a minor's year does not count. A later teacher (an אמורא) normally would not just repeat a משנה, so his statement looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: And did רב הונא come to teach us a משנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a side challenge from the answer in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that one cannot make a חזקה on a minor's property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה already implies the rule, רב הונא's statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Two answers: רב הונא states what the משנה implies, or he adds 'even if he grew up'
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the משנה does not say the rule outright, and רב הונא spells out what it implies. Second answer: רב הונא adds something new, that the rule holds even after the son grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: רב הונא is stating an inference from the משנה. And if you want, say: he is teaching us the case of 'even if he grew up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers to show that רב הונא's statement is not just a repeat of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: the משנה never says this case outright. רב הונא is the one who draws it out of the משנה. Answer two: the משנה could only teach a case where the son was still a minor in the third year. רב הונא adds that even if the son had already grown up, there is still no חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one possible answer)
An inference read out of the wording

phrases.english: If you want, say:
רב הונא is stating an inference from the משנה.
And if you want, say:
he is teaching us 'even if he grew up.'
phrases.notes: He means that even if the son was already an adult during the third year, that year still does not count toward a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַב הוּנָא דִּיּוּקָא דְמַתְנִיתִין קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two answers: the rule is only implied by the משנה, or רב הונא adds a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא only repeated what the משנה says.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either he spells out what the משנה only implies, or he adds that the rule holds even after the son grows up.

steps.title: Why not build a similar split case with the owner himself, who ran away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה could have used the other person's own field. The holder ate it two years in front of the owner and one year when the owner was away because he had run off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה teach the case of his own field, and explain it as a case where the holder ate it two years in the owner's presence and one year when he was not there, because the owner ran away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main question. It tries to make a split case for 'your own field' too, which would mean the משנה did not need the father's field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 worked because one of the three years did not count. The גמרא suggests that a year when the owner was absent because he fled might also not count. If so, 'your own field' would also give a middle case, and the reason for choosing the father's field would fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: With his own (the other person's own field)
And let him explain it as a case of

phrases.english: And let him teach it with his own,
phrases.notes: Meaning the case where the field belonged to the claimant himself, the simpler case asked about in step 12.

phrases.english: and explain it as where he ate it two years in his presence
and one not in his presence,
and where he ran away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question after the side discussion about רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only the father's field allows a meaningful middle case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An owner who ran away seems to create the same kind of non-counting year, so 'your own field' would work too.

steps.title: The runaway case fails either way: fleeing for his life or fleeing over money
steps.stepSummary: If the owner fled for his life, the case is obvious, since he could not protest. If he fled over money, he should have protested from far away, because a protest made when the holder is not present still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he run away? If he ran away for his life, it is obvious that the holder is not believed, because the owner could not protest. And if he ran away over money, he should have protested, because we hold that a protest made outside the holder's presence is still a protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion in step 19. Neither kind of runaway owner produces a case that is both real and worth teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא runs the either-or test on the runaway owner. If he fled for his life, he obviously could not protest, so it is too obvious for the משנה to teach. If he fled over money, he could have protested from afar and did not, so the holder has a valid חזקה. The father's field is still the only good middle case.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of danger to his life
A protest (declaring that the field is still his)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה used the father's field because only it gives a real middle case: two years with the father and one with the minor son, which is no חזקה under רב הונא. A runaway owner does not work. If he fled for his life the case is obvious, and if he fled over money he could have protested from afar.

phrases.english: He ran away because of what?
If he ran away because of danger to life,
it is obvious that he is not believed,
phrases.notes: The one not believed is the person holding the field, who claims he bought it.

phrases.english: since he cannot protest.
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is the owner who fled. The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: And if he ran away because of money,
he should have protested.
For we hold:
a protest not in his presence is a protest.
phrases.notes: 'His presence' means the presence of the person using the field. The owner could protest wherever he is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative case proposed in step 19, using the same either-or test as step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Either-or test showing the suggested case fails
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A runaway owner could create a non-counting year with 'your own field.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Fleeing for his life makes the case obvious. Fleeing over money leaves the חזקה valid because he could have protested from afar. So only the father's field works.

steps.title: The source: the 'three lands' for חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה listing three separate lands for חזקה. A holder in one land does not gain חזקה against an owner in another land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: There are three lands for חזקה: יהודה, עבר הירדן, and גליל. If the owner was in יהודה and someone held his field in גליל, or the owner was in גליל and someone held his field in יהודה, it is not a חזקה, until the holder is with the owner in the same land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that stands behind the idea from step 20, that a protest made away from the holder still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding a field for three years normally creates a חזקה, because the owner would have protested if it was really his. This משנה says that does not work when the owner lives in a different one of the three lands. The next steps explain how this משנה connects to the question of a protest made away from the holder.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Three lands: separate regions of ארץ ישראל
Being presumed the owner after holding and using a field for three years
He held and used the field

phrases.english: As we learned: there are three lands regarding חזקה:
Judea, Transjordan, and the Galilee.
If the owner was in Judea and someone held the field in the Galilee,
or the owner was in the Galilee and someone held it in Judea —
it is not a חזקה,
until he is with him in the same land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for step 20's claim that a protest made when the holder is not present counts.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a protest made when the holder is not present counts as a protest.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the three lands for חזקה, as the following steps explain it.

steps.title: Either view seems to clash with the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an old difficulty with the three-lands משנה. If a protest made away from the holder counts, why not across lands? If it does not count, why does it help within the same land?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What does this תנא hold? If he holds that a protest made when the holder is not present counts, then even between יהודה and גליל it should count. And if he holds that such a protest does not count, then even within יהודה it should not count!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא remembers a difficulty it once raised about this משנה. It looks as if the משנה fits neither view about a protest made away from the holder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a protest away from the holder counts, the owner in יהודה could protest about his field in גליל, so his silence should allow a חזקה. If it does not count, being in the same land should not help either, since the holder still did not hear it. Either way, splitting the country into lands seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (raised a difficulty about it)
A protest by the owner against the holder
Not in his presence, meaning the holder is not there

phrases.english: And we discussed it: what does he hold?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר מֶחָאָה שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה —
phrases.english: If he holds that a protest not in his presence is a protest —
then even in Judea and Galilee as well.
phrases.notes: He means the owner's protest from another land should also count, so the holder should gain a חזקה there too if no protest came.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי קָסָבַר מֶחָאָה שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו לָא הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה —
phrases.english: And if he holds that a protest not in his presence is not a protest —
then even Judea and Judea should also not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a difficulty with the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three-lands משנה's split between different lands and the same land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: under either view about a protest made away from the holder, the difference between lands disappears.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר ממל: the משנה speaks of a time of danger
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל says the תנא holds that a protest made away from the holder counts. The משנה is speaking about a time of danger, when no message can get through.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said: Really, he holds that a protest made when the holder is not present counts, and the משנה was taught about a time of danger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל answers the difficulty. He picks the first view and explains the משנה in a way that fits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a protest made far away counts, because word of it reaches the holder. In a time of danger, messages cannot pass between the lands, so the owner's silence proves nothing and the holder gets no חזקה. This is the source for step 20's claim that a protest away from the holder counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of danger, when travel and messages are blocked
The אמורא who gives this answer

steps.whatToRemember: A protest made when the holder is not present counts as a protest. The three-lands rule applies only in a time of danger, when news cannot travel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said:
Really, he holds
that a protest not in his presence is a protest,
and our משנה was taught about a time of danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the משנה is placed in a special situation, a time of danger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three-lands rule seemed to fit neither view about a protest made away from the holder.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a protest counts, but in a time of danger no news gets through, so there is no חזקה.

steps.title: Why mention יהודה and גליל?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is danger, why does the משנה name separate lands like יהודה and גליל? Danger could block messages inside one land too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about יהודה and גליל, that the משנה chose them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא בר ממל's answer. The answer to this question comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the real issue is danger, the dividing line between lands should not matter. Messages could be blocked between two towns in the same land. So why does the משנה build its rule around different lands?

phrases.english: And what is different about Judea and Galilee, that he mentioned them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 23 based on the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא בר ממל's claim that the משנה speaks of a time of danger.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If danger is the reason, the משנה's split by lands seems pointless, since danger can block messages within one land too.
